apertures.title: Megacolon in Myotonic Dystrophy Caused by a Degenerative Neuropathy of the Myenteric Plexus
apertures.scalar_thesis: ENS degeneration alone causes total system failure despite intact muscle, mucosa, and connective tissue. The enteric plexus is the sole functional determinant.
apertures.clinical_relevance: Proves that the tissue medicine ignores (myenteric plexus) holds the entire functional signature.

apertures.title: Stroke Alters the Function of Enteric Neurons to Impair Smooth Muscle Relaxation and Dysregulates Gut Transit
apertures.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
apertures.scalar_thesis: Stroke activates the sympathetic nervous system, which suppresses nNOS in myenteric neurons, directly poisoning the enteric substrate. Chemical sympathectomy restores function.
apertures.clinical_relevance: Stroke rehabilitation must address sympathetic overdrive to preserve enteric function. The CNS attacks the ENS directly.

apertures.title: Connecting the Dots: The Interplay Between Stroke and the Gut-Brain Axis

apertures.clinical_relevance: Stroke outcomes can be improved by addressing gut dysbiosis pre- and post-event. The gut participates in determining brain damage severity.

apertures.title: Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction with severe neuropsychiatric symptoms after total colectomy: a case report
apertures.scalar_thesis: Total colectomy in a patient with no psychiatric history produced depression, anxiety, cognitive decline, and drug-overdose behavior. All symptoms resolved with SCFA nutritional restoration.
apertures.clinical_relevance: Intestinal resection is a scalar decoupling procedure, not merely digestive surgery. Post-colectomy psychiatric symptoms are enteric decoupling syndrome, not adjustment disorder.
